q: 201. In the case of unsewered areas, an additional provision for septic tank is usually
explain: Standard estimating norms suggest 3% to 4% of the total building cost is allocated for sanitary works like septic tanks in unsewered regions.

q: 202. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: A standard high-level or low-level flushing cistern has a capacity of approximately 12.5 to 15 liters.

q: 203. The minimum size of the pipe connected to septic tank is
explain: To prevent clogging and ensure smooth flow of solids, the inlet/outlet pipes for a septic tank must be at least 100 mm (4 inches) in diameter.

q: 204. Which of the following is known as job overhead?
explain: Job overheads are site-specific expenses; insurance for workmen on that specific site is a classic example.

q: 205. The quantity of metal required, in cubic metres, for a 3.7 m wide road of one km long for one layer of compacted thickness 9 cm is
explain: Volume = Length (1000m) × Width (3.7m) × Thickness (0.09m) × 1.33 (shrinkage factor for stone metal). $1000 	imes 3.7 	imes 0.09 	imes 1.33 approx 444$.

q: 206. In standard notation which of the following is prismoidal formula for earthwork calculations
explain: The prismoidal formula (Simpson's Rule) for volume between two sections with a mid-section area $A_m$ is $V =  rac{L}{6}(A_1 + 4A_m + A_2)$.

q: 207. Approximate weight of 1 cubic metre of sand is
explain: Dry sand has a bulk density of approximately $1600 	ext{ kg/m}^3$.

q: 208. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement (C), steel (S) and coarse aggregate (A) in the increasing order
explain: Specific weights roughly: Wood (600-800), Cement (1440), Coarse Aggregate (1600-1800), Steel (7850). Order: W < C < A < S.

q: 209. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: By definition, 1 Hectare is the area of a square with 100m sides: $100 	imes 100 = 10,000 	ext{ m}^2$.

q: 210. One hectare-metre represents a volume of
explain: Volume = Area (1 Hectare) × Depth (1 m) = $10,000 	ext{ m}^2 	imes 1 	ext{ m} = 10,000 	ext{ m}^3$.

q: 211. The unit of measurement of brick work in arches is
explain: Brickwork in arches requires specialized labor and shuttering, but the quantity of material is still calculated by volume in cubic meters (m³).

q: 212. The unit of measurement of fair face brick work is
explain: Fair face brickwork refers to the outer finish or 'pointing' of the bricks where aesthetics matter. Since it is a surface treatment, it is measured in cubic meters (m^3).

q: 213. What is the minimum period for which the lime concrete in foundation be left wet without the construction of masonry over it?
explain: Lime concrete sets slowly compared to cement concrete. It must be kept moist (cured) for at least 7 days to gain sufficient strength before masonry loads are applied.

q: 214. In the centre line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the centre line length at each junction?
explain: In the center-line method, the junction where a cross wall meets a main wall results in double counting a small square. To correct this, half the breadth of the wall is deducted for every 'T' junction.

q: 215. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D/3 [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (also known as Simpson's rule for volume) uses the coefficients 1, 4, 2, 4... 1. It is expressed as $V = \frac{D}{3} [A_1 + A_n + 4(\text{even areas}) + 2(\text{remaining odd areas})]$.

q: 216. In what units are the quantities for the frames of doors and windows computed
explain: Door and window frames (Chaukhats) are made of timber and are measured by their total volume in cubic meters (m³).

q: 217. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the work at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is hired when the original contractor defaults. The cost of this second agency is 'debited' (charged) to the original contractor's account/security deposit.

q: 218. The value of a property is the amount of money whose annual interest at the highest prevailing rate of interest will be equal to the net income from the property.
explain: Capitalized Value = Net Annual Income × Year's Purchase. It represents the capital sum that would yield the property's income if invested at the current interest rate.

q: 219. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: For ergonomic use by adults, the standard rim height for a pedestal or wall-hung washbasin is between 75 cm and 80 cm from the finished floor.

q: 220. 1 Metric horse power is equal to
explain: While 1 Mechanical HP is 745.7W (rounded to 746W), 1 Metric HP (PS) is approximately 735.5W (rounded to 736W).

q: 221. The correct relationship between rise, R and tread, T is
explain: A standard rule of thumb for comfortable stair design is that twice the rise plus the tread (in mm) should equal approximately 600 mm (2R + T = 600).

q: 222. The depth of foundation for construction residential building in Kathmandu Valley is taken as
explain: Due to the soil profile and standard practice for light residential structures in Kathmandu, a foundation depth of 1.5m (approx. 5 ft) is common to reach stable strata.

q: 223. The provision for annual repair and maintenance cost of building is
explain: For government and public buildings, a budget of 1% to 1.5% of the original construction cost is usually allocated annually for routine maintenance.

q: 224. The normal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are
explain: In standard PWD specifications, the 'lead' (horizontal distance) is 30m and 'lift' (vertical distance) is 1.5m. Anything beyond this requires extra payment.

q: 225. The quantity of damp proof course (D.P.C.) is worked out in
explain: D.P.C. is a thin layer applied horizontally over walls. Since the thickness is specified and constant (e.g., 2.5 cm), it is measured by area in square meters (m²).

q: 226. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: According to IS 1200, small openings like holes for pipes or vents up to 0.1 m² (1000 sq. cm) are not deducted from the total masonry volume.

q: 227. When not specified, the volume of steel in R.C.C. work is taken as
explain: For general preliminary estimation of a whole building, the total steel consumption is often estimated at 0.6% to 1% of the concrete volume.

q: 228. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass work, whether it is for supply, fixing, or cleaning, is calculated based on the surface area in square meters (sq. m).

q: 229. The process of evaluating cost of construction of a project is called
explain: Estimating is the technical process of determining the probable cost of a project based on its dimensions and prevailing rates.

q: 230. While estimating for lintels over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: The 'bearing' is the part of the lintel that rests on the wall. The standard rule is to use the thickness of the lintel itself, but it should never be less than 12 cm.

q: 231. While estimating for plastering usually no deduction is made for
explain: Small surface interruptions like beam ends, rafter ends, or tiny openings are not deducted because the labor saved is offset by the labor required to finish the edges.

q: 232. Pick up the item of work not included in the plinth area estimate
explain: The plinth area includes the covered built-up area. Courtyards are open-to-sky spaces and are therefore excluded.

q: 233. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: If the total expenditure on a work is likely to exceed the original technical sanction by more than 5%, a Revised Estimate must be prepared.

q: 234. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate must account for the volume of material, its market availability, and the cost to transport it to the site (lead charges).

q: 235. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: For large projects, 2% to 3% of the total estimated cost is often set aside for departmental supervision and quality control.

q: 236. Estimate expected to be least accurate is
explain: Plinth area estimates are preliminary/approximate estimates based on previous similar works. They lack the precision of detailed calculations.

q: 237. The useful part of liveable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area is the area where a carpet can be spread. It excludes walls and non-living spaces like corridors or lift shafts.

q: 238. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than ........... of the capital cost.
explain: If cumulative repairs exceed 2.5% of the total capital cost of the building annually, it is generally considered economically unviable.

q: 239. The ratio of cost of labour to the total cost of the building is
explain: In standard construction, material accounts for about 75% and labor for about 25% (a 1:4 ratio) of the total project cost.

q: 240. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: Standard Gauge 25 (SWG) for metal sheets corresponds to approximately 0.5 mm, which is less than 1 mm.

q: 241. In the detailed estimate the areas are worked out to the nearest
explain: According to measurement rules, areas should be calculated and rounded to the nearest 0.01 square meter.

q: 242. In the detailed estimate the volumes are worked out to the nearest
explain: Similar to area, volumetric measurements in estimation books are typically rounded to the nearest 0.01 cubic meter.

q: 243. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies (usually 3% to 5%) are added to an estimate to cover incidental expenses or unforeseen changes during construction.

q: 244. The size of the standard modular brick is
explain: The actual size of a modular brick is 19 x 9 x 9 cm. When mortar joints (1 cm) are added, the nominal size becomes 20 x 10 x 10 cm.

q: 245. The number of standard modular bricks required to make 1 m³ of masonry is
explain: Using the nominal size (20x10x10 cm), the volume of one brick is 0.002 m³. Therefore, $1 / 0.002 = 500$ bricks.

q: 246. The expected out turn of cement concrete 1 : 2 : 4 per mason per day is
explain: A mason, supported by laborers, is expected to place and finish approximately 5.0 cubic meters of mass concrete (1:2:4) in an 8-hour workday.

q: 247. The unit of measurement of roofing (each and every detail specified) is
explain: Roofing work (sheets, tiles, or slabs) is measured by the net planar area covered, expressed in square meters (m²).

q: 248. The measurement of steel grills is taken in terms of
explain: Steel products like grills, gates, and trusses are generally paid for by their weight (usually kilograms or quintals).

q: 249. Whenever the whitewashing or distempering is done on corrugated iron sheets, in the estimation the plan area the sheets is increased by
explain: Because of the 'waves' in corrugated sheets, the actual surface area is greater than the plan area. For standard GI sheets, a 14% increase is applied.

q: 250. Whenever colour washing on A.C. corrugated sheets is done, in the estimation the plan area of the sheets is increased by
explain: Asbestos Cement (A.C.) sheets have deeper corrugations than GI sheets, requiring a larger factor—usually 20%—to account for the extra surface area.

q: 251. In case of grills, for the estimation of painted area, the flat area is multiplied by
explain: To account for both sides and the intricate edges of a steel grill, the front area is doubled (multiplied by 2) to find the total painting area.

q: 252. In case of steel rolling shutters, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: Rolling shutters have a corrugated profile. To estimate the painting area for one side, the flat area is multiplied by 1.1 or 1.25 (1 1/4) depending on the corrugation depth.

q: 253. In analysis of rate, the quantity of dry mortar for 10 cubic metre brick work is taken as
explain: For 10 m³ of brickwork, approximately 3 m³ of dry mortar is needed to fill the joints after accounting for wastage and shrinkage.

q: 254. The unit of measurement of sugar is
explain: In old-style construction (like traditional lime-surkhi mortars where sugar/jaggery was an additive), such materials are measured by weight in kilograms (kg).

q: 255. The unit of measurement of electric wire
explain: Electric wires and cables are measured and sold by their length in running meters (per m).

q: 256. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having no relationship with real damage in
explain: Unliquidated damages are not predetermined in the contract; they are assessed by a court after the breach based on the actual loss suffered.

q: 257. One cubic metre of cement concrete (1 : 2 : 4) is to be mixed by volume. Number of cement bags required will be approximately
explain: For 1:2:4 concrete, 1.52 m³ of dry material is needed. Cement volume = $1.52 / (1+2+4) = 0.217 \text{ m}^3$. Since 1 bag = 0.0347 m³, $0.217 / 0.0347 \approx 6.2$ bags.

q: 258. The estimated quantity of cement required in cement mortar (1 : 6) per cubic metre will be
explain: Dry volume for mortar is 1.33 m³. Cement = $1.33 / 7 = 0.19 \text{ m}^3$. Number of bags = $0.19 / 0.0347 \approx 5.4$ (The closest standard answer in many keys is 4.8 to 5.0).

q: 259. Thickness of plastering is usually
explain: Standard internal plastering for brick walls is typically 12 mm thick to provide a smooth, level finish.

q: 260. One cubic metre of mild steel weights about
explain: The density of mild steel is a standard engineering constant: 7,850 kilograms per cubic meter ($7850 \text{ kg/m}^3$).
